context: Hiroshi-elder talks to Hina-young about old village customs.
purpose: Elder passing rural cultural memory to teen.

lines.speaker: hina_child
lines.jp: おじいちゃん、村の話、聞きたい。
lines.en: Grandpa, will you tell me about the village? The stories from back then?
lines.style: Bright, eager opening — leaning forward. Respectful but unselfconscious. A child who feels safe asking. Warm, unhurried pace.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: 昔の村は、ようけ習慣あった。
lines.en: The old village had so many customs, you know.
lines.style: Settling into memory. Soft Kansai cadence. Each word lands gently, like placing something precious down. Not teaching — sharing. Slight smile in the voice.

lines.speaker: hina_child
lines.style: Quick, interested follow-up. No hesitation — she trusts he'll know what she means. Open, eager to listen. Genuine curiosity, not performing it.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.en: Setsubun, mochi pounding, rice planting — the seasonal festivals and the work that came with them.
lines.style: Rhythmic listing, gentle. Slight pause between each one — letting them sit. Kansai warmth underneath. Voice of someone conjuring the past without strain.

lines.speaker: hina_child
lines.en: Do people still do those things now?
lines.style: Genuine question, searching. Soft voice but real concern underneath — wondering if something she values will survive. Leaning in slightly.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: 少しはな、でも減ってる。
lines.en: Some of it, yes… but it's fading away, I'm afraid.
lines.style: Honest, without heaviness. A small sigh folded in. Regret that doesn't ask for comfort. Kansai gentleness. Matter-of-fact acceptance mixed with quiet loss.

lines.speaker: hina_child
lines.en: Then I want to tell people about it — the young people especially. I want to pass it on.
lines.style: Sudden steadiness and resolve. Still soft-spoken, but conviction underneath. Not demanding — offering. The voice of someone who has just decided something matters enough to say.
